context: Planning next week’s stall location over closing chat
purpose: Plan the next market; teach 売り/最低/わずか/トラブル/つくる/売る/づくり

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 来週の売り場、場所変えよか。
lines.en: Should we change the stall spot next week?
lines.style: pondering Kansai owner weighing a move

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.jp: いいですね。最低でも今より広い所がいい。
lines.en: Good idea. At least somewhere bigger than now.
lines.style: eager assistant pushing for more space

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: わずかでも家賃上がるとつらいけどな。
lines.en: Even a tiny rent increase would sting, though.
lines.style: budget-conscious owner wary of cost, each word carrying genuine natural feeling

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.jp: トラブルが少ない場所を選びましょう。
lines.en: Let us pick a place with fewer problems.
lines.style: sensible helper prioritizing a calm spot

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 商品、もっとつくる必要あるな。
lines.en: We need to make more products.
lines.style: planning craftsman thinking about supply, voice clear and distinctly their own

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.jp: 手づくりの良さが売りですもんね。
lines.en: The handmade quality is our selling point, after all.
lines.style: affirming helper naming the stall’s strength

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: せや、それが一番売れる理由や。
lines.en: Right, that is the biggest reason they sell.
lines.style: agreeing owner proud of his craft

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 残り全部、夏までに売るつもりや。
lines.en: I plan to sell all the rest by summer.
lines.style: ambitious Kansai owner setting a deadline
